title: Mexico Says Fourth USMCA Round Postponed Indefinitely as Xi Jinping's Washington Visit Takes Priority
detail: Mexico's deputy economy minister for foreign trade, Luis Rosendo Gutierrez, told reporters the fourth bilateral US-Mexico USMCA negotiating round — previously expected the week of Sept 28 in Washington — will not take place next week, with October now the most likely window, though no new date was set. Gutierrez cited scheduling conflicts including Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington and the upcoming G20 summit, saying 'we agreed with the United States that in the coming weeks we will announce when the fourth round will take place.' He said the two sides' technical agenda has expanded from 54 to nearly 90 discrete issues even as formal rounds pause, with USTR staff and Mexican negotiators continuing daily technical coordination. Mexico's stated priority remains 'reducing Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum and automobiles.'

media.caption: Mexico's deputy economy minister says the fourth USMCA round has been postponed amid Xi Jinping's Washington visit
